comments.content: The nested conditional types here are misleading and partly dead: since `Nullable<T>` is just `T | null`, `Selectable<DB[T]> extends Nullable<infer N>` and `O extends Nullable<infer N>` always match, so the non-null `: Selectable<DB[T]>` / `: O` branches can never be selected. The result is effectively `Selectable<DB[T]> | null` / `O | null`, which is also what a left-joined `toJson` actually produces at runtime. Simplifying avoids the deeply nested ternaries (discouraged by the project style rules) and makes the intent (top-level nullable, properties non-nullable) explicit.
comments.suggestion_code: Simplify<T extends TB ? Selectable<DB[T]> | null : T extends Expression<infer O> ? O | null : never>
comments.existing_code:
Simplify<
      T extends TB
        ? Selectable<DB[T]> extends Nullable<infer N>
          ? N | null
          : Selectable<DB[T]>
        : T extends Expression<infer O>
          ? O extends Nullable<infer N>
            ? N | null
            : O
          : never
    >
